SIBAWAYH:وذاكلأنهاظروففيهاالأشياءوتكونفي.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذاكلأنهاظروففيهاالأشياءوتكونفي.speaker: حميد الأرقط
SIBAWAYH:وذاكلأنهاظروففيهاالأشياءوتكونفي.claim: The rājiz Hamīd al-Arqaṭ uses مثل كعصف مأكول in poetry, illustrating the poetic extension of ك after مثل.
SIBAWAYH:وذاكلأنهاظروففيهاالأشياءوتكونفي.anchor: حميد الأرقط # % فصيروا مثل كعصف مأكول

BURSEVI:v10p400/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p400/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p400/r6.claim: ʿAṣf is cut plant foliage, often eaten by worms; the birds' attack left the army ruined, pierced, and dispersed like worm-eaten crops.
BURSEVI:v10p400/r6.anchor: كورق زرع وقع فيه الآكال وهو أن يأكله الدود وسمى ورق الزرع بالعصف لأن شأنه أن يقطع

BURSEVI:v10p400/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p400/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p400/r7.claim: Other readings compare them to crops whose grain has been eaten, leaving empty straw, or to dung that dries and breaks apart, evoking lost lives and dismembered bodies.
BURSEVI:v10p400/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى كورق زرع أكل حبه فبقى صفرا منه

BURSEVI:v10p400/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p400/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p400/r8.claim: Calling them eaten straw is a decorous euphemism for refuse, as the Qur'an says messengers ate food instead of naming bodily functions.
BURSEVI:v10p400/r8.anchor: إلا أنه عبر عن الرجيع بالمأكول أو أشير إليه بأول حاله على طريق الكناية

BURSEVI:v10p400/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p400/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p400/r9.claim: A person who relies on anything besides God may be destroyed through the weakest creature; the elephant army trusted its elephant, but birds overcame it.
BURSEVI:v10p400/r9.anchor: قال بعض العارفين من كان اعتماده على غير الله أهلكه الله بأضعف خلقه ألا ترى أن أصحاب الفيل

QASHANI:105:3-5/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:105:3-5/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:105:3-5/r3.claim: The troops become inert like consumed straw: discipline kills the vegetative powers and removes their capacity and characteristic force.
QASHANI:105:3-5/r3.anchor: كقوى نباتية أميتت وذهبت قوتها وخاصيتها ووقفت عن فعلها لضعفها بالرياضة

QUSHAYRI:v3p449/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p449/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p449/r14.claim: “Eaten straw” means the ends of crops before ripening, while “eaten” refers to their fruit having been consumed.
QUSHAYRI:v3p449/r14.anchor: فجعلهم كعصف مأكول } . { كعصف } : كأطراف الزرع قبل أن يدرك . ( مأكول )

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3466#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3466#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3466#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas likens the defeated army to chaff from crops eaten by birds.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3466#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس كعصف ماكول قال : هو الطيور غصافة الزرع

IBNASHUR:105:5/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:105:5/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:105:5/r1.claim: ʿAṣf is the leaf of a crop and a collective plural of ʿaṣfah.

IBNASHUR:105:5/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:105:5/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:105:5/r2.claim: When livestock eat crop leaves, they trample them, consume their edges, then leave them scattered on the ground, once lush and green.
IBNASHUR:105:5/r2.anchor: والعصف إذا دخلته البهائم فأكلته داسته بأرجلها وأكلت أطرافه وطرحته على الأرض بعد أن كان أخضر يانعا

IBNASHUR:105:5/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:105:5/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:105:5/r3.claim: This image compares the People of the Elephant, after their bloom and strength, to fallen dead remains.
IBNASHUR:105:5/r3.anchor: وهذا تمثيل لحال أصحاب الفيل بعد تلك النضرة والقوة كيف صاروا متساقطين على الأرض هالكين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p555/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p555/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p555/r2.claim: Al-Farra and Ibn Ishaq connect “for Quraysh's protection” to al-Fil 105:5, treating the surahs as linked.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p555/r2.anchor: وجوز الفراء وابن إسحاق في ( السيرة ) أن يكون { لإيلاف قريش } متعلقا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p555/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p555/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p555/r3.claim: Al-Qurtubi says this inter-sura attachment is also Mujahid's view and a report from Ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p555/r3.anchor: قال القرطبي : وهو معنى قول مجاهد ورواية ابن جبير عن ابن عباس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p555/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p555/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p555/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari compares linking the independent surah to its predecessor with a poetic line whose meaning depends on the preceding line.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p555/r4.anchor: قال الزمخشري : وهذا بمنزلة التضمين في الشعر وهو أن يتعلق معنى البيت بالذي قبله تعلقا لا يصح إلا به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#2/r6.claim: The army retreated toward Yemen and died in scattered stages; Abraha’s fingers decayed one by one, while God protected His sanctified House, showing that all power belongs to Him and idols were powerless.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#2/r6.anchor: فانصرف أبرهة بمن معه يريد اليمن فماتوا في طريقهم متفرقين في كل مرحلة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#3/r4.claim: Asf is wheat’s leaves and straw; a line by ‘Alqama ibn ‘Abada illustrates the term. The army became like eaten, excreted straw, combining degradation and destruction.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#3/r5.speaker: أبو الخليج الهذلي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#3/r5.claim: Abu al-Khalij al-Hudhali reads the clause as ‘and He left them like eaten straw.’

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#3/r6.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#3/r6.claim: ‘Ikrima defines asf as wheat grains that become hollow after being eaten.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#3/r6.anchor: وقال عكرمة: العصف حب البر إذا أكل فصار أجوف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#3/r7.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#3/r7.claim: Al-Farra’ says asf is the tips of plants before they form ears.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#3/r7.anchor: وقال الفراء: هو أطراف الزرع قبل أن يسنبل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#3/r8.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#3/r8.claim: In Ubayy ibn Ka‘b’s codex, this surah is joined directly to the Quraysh surah; Sufyan ibn ‘Uyayna says an imam he knew recited them as a single surah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p523#3/r8.anchor: وهذه السورة متصلة في مصحف أبي بن كعب بسورة لإيلاف قريش لا فصل بينهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p236#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p236#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p236#4/r1.claim: The author directs readers to his explanation of ʿaṣf in Sura al-Rahman.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p236#4/r1.anchor: ومعنى العصف في سورة [ الرحمن 12 ] عز وجل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p236#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p236#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p236#4/r2.claim: One view says the grain inside the plant was eaten, leaving a husk without grain.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p236#4/r2.anchor: أحدهما أن يكون أراد أنه أخذ ما فيه من الحب فأكل وبقي هو لا حب فيه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p236#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p236#4/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p236#4/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains it as plant matter eaten by animals, with the word used for what is edible just as one names drinkable water for drinking.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p236#4/r3.anchor: والثاني أن يكون أراد أن العصف مأكول البهائم كما يقال للحنطة هذا المأكول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p236#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p236#4/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p236#4/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says it is like dry crop leaves marked by gnawing or decay.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p236#4/r4.anchor: والثالث أن المأكول هاهنا الذي وقع فيه الأكال فالمعنى جعلهم كورق الزرع الذي جف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p483#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p483#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p483#2/r2.claim: The event was a portent before the Prophet’s mission; Muhammad was born that year according to the most widely held view, and God protected the House He would honor through the final unlettered prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p483#2/r2.anchor: فإنه في ذلك العام ولد على أشهر الأقوال، ولسان حال القدر يقول: لم ننصركم -يا معشر قريش-على الحبشة لخيريتكم عليهم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p486#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p486#2/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p486#2/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the Prophet reminded Quraysh that God’s rescue preserved their political continuity and the security and provision named in Surah Quraysh, so they might accept the good offered them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p486#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: فلما بعث الله محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم كان فيما يعد به على قريش من نعمته (3) عليهم وفضله،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p486#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p486#2/r4.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p486#2/r4.claim: Ibn Hisham glosses abābīl as groups without an Arabic singular, sijjīl as hard and strong or a Persian combination of stone and clay, and ʿaṣf as uncut crop foliage.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p486#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن هشام: الأبابيل الجماعات، ولم تتكلم العرب بواحدة. قال: وأما السجيل، فأخبرني يونس النحوي وأبو عبيدة أنه عند العرب: الشديد الصلب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr glosses ʿaṣf as straw, wheat leaves, or straw generally; maʾkūl means fodder cut for animals, as al-Hasan also says.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r1.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: يعني التبن الذي تسميه العامة: هبور. وفي رواية عن سعيد: ورق الحنطة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says ʿaṣf is the husk surrounding a grain, like the covering on wheat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: العصف: القشرة التي على الحبة، كالغلاف على الحنطة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says ʿaṣf is crop or vegetable foliage after animals eat and excrete it as dung.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r3.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: العصف: ورق الزرع، وورق البقل، إذا أكلته البهائم فراثته، فصار درينا (3)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir summarizes that God destroyed the army, frustrated its plan, and killed most; wounded Abraha reached Sanaʿa and died when his chest split open.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r4.anchor: والمعنى: أن الله، سبحانه وتعالى، أهلكهم ودمرهم، وردهم بكيدهم وغيظهم لم ينالوا خيرا،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r5.claim: After Abraha died, his sons Yaksum and Masruq ruled; Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan sought Persian aid, restored Himyarite rule, and received Arab delegations of congratulations.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p488/r5.anchor: فملك بعده ابنه يكسوم، ثم من بعده أخوه مسروق بن أبرهة (1) ثم خرج سيف بن ذي يزن الحميري إلى كسرى

FARRA:v3p291#2/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p291#2/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p291#2/r4.claim: God sent birds carrying stones like sheep droppings; each stone struck its owner’s head and exited through the anus, killing them all.
FARRA:v3p291#2/r4.anchor: قد بعث الله تبارك وتعالى عليهم طيرا في مناقيرها الحجارة كبعر الغنم،

FARRA:v3p291#2/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p291#2/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p291#2/r8.claim: ʿAṣf means the crop’s tips before it ripens and heads out.
FARRA:v3p291#2/r8.anchor:
وقوله عز وجل: كعصف (5) .
والعصف: أطراف الزرع قبل أن يدرك ويسنبل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p489/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p489/r2.speaker: أبو قيس بن الأسلت الأنصاري المري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p489/r2.claim: His poem recalls the elephant episode: the army was routed, an elephant was injured, and a showering wind scattered them like small bundles.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p489/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p489/r3.speaker: أبو الصلت بن أبي ربيعة الثقفي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p489/r3.claim: The poem says the elephant was immobilized at al-Mughammis, the force fled with broken legs, and the event remains among God's signs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p489/r3.anchor: حبس الفيل بالمغمس حتى … صار يحبو،

KASHSHAF:105:4/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:105:4/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:105:4/r6.claim: The people were likened to crop leaves eaten away, that is, damaged by feeding insects.
KASHSHAF:105:4/r6.anchor: وشبهوا بورق الزرع إذا أكل ،   أي : وقع فيه الأكال .

KASHSHAF:105:5/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:105:5/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:105:5/r1.claim: ‘Eaten’ may mean eaten by worms, or straw eaten and excreted by livestock; the latter wording follows Qurʾanic decorum, as in the verse saying the two ate food.
KASHSHAF:105:5/r1.anchor: أي : وقع فيه الأكال ،   وهو أن يأكله الدود .

KASHSHAF:105:5/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:105:5/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:105:5/r2.claim: Alternatively, the grain was eaten, leaving only an empty husk.
KASHSHAF:105:5/r2.anchor: أو أريد : أكل حبه فبقي صفراً منه .

KASHSHAF:105:5/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:105:5/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF:105:5/r3.claim: A merit report says reciting al-Fīl protects a person during life from being swallowed by the earth or transformed.
KASHSHAF:105:5/r3.anchor: من قرأ سورة الفيل أعفاه الله أيام حياته من الخسف والمسخ

MAJAZ:v2p312/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p312/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p312/r3.claim: ʿAṣf is crop foliage, also called ʿaṣīfa.
MAJAZ:v2p312/r3.anchor: «كعصف مأكول» (5) وهو ورق الزرع هو العصيفة.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says eaten straw is plant foliage consumed by worms.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.anchor: أحدها : أن العصف ورق الزرع , والمأكول الذي قد أكله الدود , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r2.speaker: حسين بن ثابت
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r2.claim: Husayn ibn Thabit says eaten straw means food.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r2.anchor: الثاني : أن العصف المأكول هو الطعام , وهذا قول حسين بن ثابت .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r3.speaker: عطاء بن السائب
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r3.claim: A report from Ata ibn al-Saib identifies it as the wheat husk after its contents are eaten.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r3.anchor: الثالث : أنه قشر الحنطة إذا أكل ما فيه , رواه عطاء بن السائب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says it is vegetable foliage after livestock eat and excrete it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r4.anchor: الرابع : أنه ورق البقل إذا أكلته البهائم فراثته , قاله ابن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r5.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Hasan interpret straw as figs and what was eaten as fodder for animals.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p343#2/r5.anchor: الخامس : أن العصف التين والمأكول القصيل للدواب , قاله سعيد بن جبير والحسن , واختلف فيما فعله الله بهم

MUJAHID:v2p784/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p784/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p784/r1.claim: Mujahid says the chaff is wheat leaves.
MUJAHID:v2p784/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ كعصف مأكول ﴾ العصف ورق الحنطة

MUJAHID:v2p784/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p784/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MUJAHID:v2p784/r2.claim: Sa‘id ibn Jubayr glosses the chaff as al-habur.
MUJAHID:v2p784/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال العصف هو الهبور

MUQATIL:105:1-5#3/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:105:1-5#3/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:105:1-5#3/r7.claim: The invaders are compared to eaten chaff, meaning decayed crop leaves. The army was destroyed forty years before the Prophet's birth at the edge of the sanctuary and never entered it.
MUQATIL:105:1-5#3/r7.anchor: فشبههم بورق الزرع المأكول يعني البالي، وكان أصحاب الفيل قبل مولد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأربعين سنة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p357#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p357#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p357#5/r1.claim: They were made like crop straw eaten by worms.

NAHHAS:v5p291/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p291/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p291/r10.claim: The kāf is a second object; maʾkūl means the husk of wheat, or something eaten by livestock.
NAHHAS:v5p291/r10.anchor: الكاف في موضع نصب مفعول ثان أي مأكول ما فيه وهو قشر الحنطة

QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r1.claim: God made the army like crop leaves chewed and discarded by livestock; their severed, scattered limbs resemble fragments of the plant.
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r1.anchor: أي جعل الله أصحاب الفيل كورق الزرع إذا أكلته الدواب

QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd and others transmit the explanation that the simile depicts the army’s body parts scattered like eaten leaves.
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r2.anchor: شبه تقطع أوصالهم بتفرق أجزائه. روي معناه عن ابن زيد وغيره

QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r3.claim: The noun عصف has forms عصفة, عصافة, and عصيفة; a verse by ʿAlqama supports the meaning “crop leaf.”
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r3.anchor: العصف: جمع، واحدته عصفة، وعصافة، وعصيفة

QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r4.claim: The prefixed kāf in كعصف adds comparison despite the presence of مثل, just as in the wording of 42:11.
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r4.anchor: وأدخل الكاف في «كعصف» للتشبيه مع مثل، نحو قوله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r5.claim: مأكول means that the grain inside has been eaten, like calling someone “handsome” while intending his face.
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r5.anchor: ومعنى «مأكول» مأكول حبه. كما يقال: فلان حسن أي حسن وجهه

QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the simile as wheat husk; a report says stones burst open the victims and left them like a husk stripped of its kernel.
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس «فجعلهم كعصف مأكول» أن المراد به قشر البر

QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿud says God sent wind that intensified the stones, making every struck person die; his account includes a Kinda survivor’s poem.
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r7.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: لما رمت الطير بالحجارة، بعث الله ريحا

QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r8.claim: Other reports say the birds did not strike everyone, while the commander and a small band escaped but died after describing the punishment; Qurtubi leaves the matter to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r8.anchor: ويروى أنها لم تصبهم كلهم، لكنها أصابت من شاء الله منهم

QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r9.speaker: ابن إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r9.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the Arabs thereafter regarded Quraysh as God’s people because God fought the invaders for them.
QURTUBI-FULL:105:5/r9.anchor: لما رد الله الحبشة عن مكة، عظمت العرب قريشا وقالوا

QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r1.claim: ʿAṣf is dry foliage; eaten foliage is crushed into crumbs, whether chewed by insects or ground by an animal, portraying bodily disintegration from the stones.

QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r2.claim: Qutb says there is no need to reinterpret the image as destruction by smallpox or measles.
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r2.anchor: ولا ضرورة لتأويلها بأنها تصوير لحال هلاكهم بمرض الجدري أو الحصبة

QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r3.claim: God did not entrust the sanctuary's protection to the polytheists: He let them be defeated so they would not claim credit, then intervened openly to proclaim His protection.
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r3.anchor: لم يرد أن يكل حماية بيته

QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r4.claim: This intervention should have led Quraysh and the Arabs to accept Islam when the Messenger came, rather than let pride in sanctuary service and idolatry block them; the reminder rebukes their stubbornness.
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r4.anchor: أن تبادر قريش ويبادر العرب إلى الدخول في دين الله

QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r5.claim: God kept the sanctuary and holy land beyond the control of the People of the Book despite its pagan custodians, preserving it as a free cradle for the coming faith.
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r5.anchor: أن يحطموا البيت الحرام أو يسيطروا على الأرض المقدسة

QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r6.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r6.claim: Qutb applies the lesson to his own era, expressing hope that God will protect the sacred sites and Medina from international Crusader and Zionist designs.

QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r7.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r7.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r7.claim: Before Islam the Arabs lacked political weight: Yemen was under Persian or Abyssinian power, the north under Rome, and central Arabia remained divided or pastoral; the Elephant year showed their weakness against foreign invasion.

QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r8.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r8.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r8.claim: Arabs gained an international role by identifying as Muslims and following Islam alone, rather than elevating ethnic or tribal chauvinism.

QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r9.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r9.speaker: ربعي بن عامر
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r9.claim: At Yazdegerd's court, the Muslim envoy summarized the mission as freeing people from worship of people to worship of God, from worldly constriction to the Hereafter's breadth, and from oppressive religions to Islam's justice.
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r9.anchor: كما قال ربعي بن عامر رسول المسلمين في مجلس يزدجرد :  " الله ابتعثنا لنخرج الناس من عبادة العباد

QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r10.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r10.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r10.claim: Arab strength and leadership endured while they upheld Islam; when they returned to ethnic and tribal banners, other nations subdued them because they abandoned God and He left them.
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r10.anchor: حتى إذا انحرفوا عنها وذكروا عنصريتهم وعصبيتهم

QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r11.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r11.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r11.claim: Qutb argues that without Islam the Arabs have no distinctive idea to offer humanity or historic role; like the Tatars and western barbarians, conquerors without a guiding idea are absorbed by the peoples they conquer.
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r11.anchor: والأمم التي لم تكن تمثل فكرة كالتتار

QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r12.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r12.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r12.claim: The surah's lesson urges Arabs to remember that their life, strength, and leadership depend on carrying Islam.
QUTB-ZILAL:105:5/r12.anchor: وهذا ما يجب أن يذكره العرب جيدا إذا هم أرادوا الحياة

RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r1.claim: Asf has several meanings: post-harvest leaves left in the field and eaten by livestock, straw dispersed from grain by wind, plant tips before grain matures, or kernels eaten leaving husks.
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r1.anchor: وذكروا ههنا وجوها : أحدها : أنه ورق الزرع الذي يبقى في الأرض بعد الحصاد

RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r2.claim: Abu Muslim specifically takes asf as straw, which wind separates from grain when winnowing; once eaten, it is spent and powerless.
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : العصف التبن لقوله : { ذو العصف والريحان }

RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل وقتادة وعطاء عن ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r3.claim: If ma'kul means eaten, one reading compares them to fodder digested and excreted by livestock, whose dried fragments disperse, like the army's dismembered bodies; this is attributed to Muqatil, Qatada, and Ata from Ibn Abbas.
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r3.anchor: وهو قول مقاتل ، وقتادة وعطاء عن ابن عباس

RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r4.claim: A second reading of eaten fodder compares the army to crop leaves damaged by worms.
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r4.anchor: أن يكون التشبيه واقعا بورق الزرع إذا وقع فيه الأكال

RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r5.claim: Hasan interprets the image as straw whose grain has been eaten, with 'eaten' grammatically attributed to the whole stalk because its meaning is understood.

RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r6.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r6.claim: Ikrima and al-Dahhak take ma'kul as edible fodder: the army became like straw fit for animals to eat.

RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r7.claim: Some object that al-Hajjaj destroyed the Kaaba without a similar event and infer that the Elephant story was different or had another cause; Razi replies that the earlier event was a harbinger before Muhammad's mission, when such a sign was needed.
RAZI-FULL:v32p96#2/r7.anchor: أنا بينا أن ذلك وقع إرهاصا لأمر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

STUDYQURAN:105:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:105:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:105:intro/r1.claim: The early Meccan surah recounts Abrahah’s 570 campaign against the Kaʿbah after he built a church in Sanʿāʾ to divert pilgrims; God repelled his army with birds and stones.
STUDYQURAN:105:intro/r1.anchor: Abrahah, an Abyssinian general who ruled Yemen, had built a church in Sanʿāʾ

STUDYQURAN:105:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:105:5/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:105:5/r1.claim: Devoured husks are animal-eaten leaf remains; the surah contrasts Arabia’s greatest army with something among its most insignificant things.
STUDYQURAN:105:5/r1.anchor: Devoured husks renders ʿāsfin maʾkūl, which indicates the remains of leaves eaten by animals

TAB-FULL:v24p643/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p643/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p643/r4.claim: Qatāda says Abraha marched from Abyssinia with Yemenis to avenge a church destroyed in Yemen; white sea birds pelted the army, and Abraha survived only to die after his flesh fell away.
TAB-FULL:v24p643/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بأصحاب الفيل} [الفيل: 1] " أقبل أبرهة الأشرم من الحبشة

TAB-FULL:v24p644/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r1.claim: God made the Elephant people like crops eaten by animals, digested, dried, and scattered, paralleling their dismembered limbs and dispersed bodies.
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r1.anchor: يعني تعالى ذكره: فجعل الله أصحاب الفيل كزرع أكلته الدواب فراثته، فيبس وتفرقت أجزاؤه؛

TAB-FULL:v24p644/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r2.claim: Another explanation takes ʿaṣf as the outer husk around a wheat grain.
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r2.anchor: وقد كان بعضهم يقول: العصف: هو القشر الخارج الذي يكون على حب الحنطة من خارج، كهيئة الغلاف لها.

TAB-FULL:v24p644/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r3.claim: Mujāhid says ʿaṣf means wheat leaves.
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: {كعصف مأكول} [الفيل: 5] قال: «ورق الحنطة»

TAB-FULL:v24p644/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says it is like eaten crops.
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r5.anchor: قال: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {كعصف مأكول} [الفيل: 5] «كزرع مأكول»

TAB-FULL:v24p644/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk also gives the Nabataean term habūr, with a variant reading maqūr.
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله {كعصف مأكول} [الفيل: 5] قال: هو الهبور بالنبطية،

TAB-FULL:v24p644/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says ʿaṣf is crop or greens leaves after beasts eat and excrete them as dung.
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {فجعلهم كعصف مأكول} [الفيل: 5] قال: «ورق الزرع وورق البقل،

TAB-FULL:v24p644/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the grain is eaten and its husk is scattered by the wind; ʿaṣf is the husk over the grain.
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r8.anchor: عن أبيه، عن ابن عباس، {كعصف مأكول} [الفيل: 5] قال: البر يؤكل ويلقي عصفه الريح

TAB-FULL:v24p644/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r9.speaker: حبيب بن أبي ثابت
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r9.claim: Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit glosses it as food that has been eaten.
TAB-FULL:v24p644/r9.anchor: عن أبي سنان، عن حبيب بن أبي ثابت: {كعصف مأكول} [الفيل: 5] قال: «كطعام مطعوم»

TAB-FULL:v24p646#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p646#2/r5.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v24p646#2/r5.claim: A Basran grammarian connects the laam to the previous sura's ending: the defeat of the elephant army was a favor to Quraysh, with the laam meaning 'for' or 'toward'.
TAB-FULL:v24p646#2/r5.anchor: فكان بعض نحويي البصرة يقول: الجالب لها قوله {فجعلهم كعصف مأكول} [الفيل: 5]

TAB-FULL:v24p650/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p650/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p650/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects linking Quraysh's laam to the previous sura: that would leave the elephant passage incomplete and contradict the consensus that these are separate complete suras.
TAB-FULL:v24p650/r1.anchor: وأما القول الذي قاله من حكينا قوله، أنه من صلة قوله: {فجعلهم كعصف مأكول} [الفيل: 5] فإن ذلك لو كان كذلك،

ZAJJAJ:v5p364/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p364/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p364/r1.claim: They were made like dry, eaten crop leaves, with rot or worms having eaten them.
ZAJJAJ:v5p364/r1.anchor: أي جعلهم كورق الزرع الذي جف وأكل: أي: وقع فيه الأكال.

ZAJJAJ:v5p364/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p364/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p364/r2.claim: Tafsir reports that God sent a flood which carried them to the sea.
ZAJJAJ:v5p364/r2.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن الله تعالى أرسل عليهم سيلا فحملهم إلى البحر

TABATABAI:105:1-5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:105:1-5/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:105:1-5/r7.claim: ʿAsf is crop foliage; eaten ʿasf is either leaves after the grain is eaten or husks after kernels are removed, depicting bodies left lifeless or guts burned by the stones' heat.
TABATABAI:105:1-5/r7.anchor: العصف ورق الزرع والعصف المأكول ورق الزرع الذي أكل حبه أو قشر الحب الذي أكل لبه

TABATABAI:105:1-5/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:105:1-5/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:105:1-5/r8.claim: Another interpretation compares them to leaves ruined by insects eating the crop.
TABATABAI:105:1-5/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد ورق الزرع الذي وقع فيها الأكال وهو أن يأكله الدود فيفسده

TABATABAI:105:1-5/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:105:1-5/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:105:1-5/r9.claim: Other interpretations of the image are rejected as inconsistent with Quranic decorum.
TABATABAI:105:1-5/r9.anchor: وفسرت الآية ببعض وجوه أخر لا يناسب الأدب القرآني

TABRISI:105:4-5/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:105:4-5/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:105:4-5/r6.claim: Asif maʾkūl is crop or straw chewed by animals, excreted, trampled, and scattered; this image compares the dismemberment of the army to scattered dung.
TABRISI:105:4-5/r6.anchor: كزرع وتبن قد أكلته الدواب ثم راثته فديست وتفرقت أجزاؤه

TABRISI:105:4-5/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:105:4-5/r7.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:105:4-5/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan says that in Medina, boys called barley shoots eaten by them ʿasif.
TABRISI:105:4-5/r7.anchor: قال الحسن: كنا ونحن غلمان بالمدينة نأكل الشعير إذا قصب وكان يسمى العصف

TABRISI:105:4-5/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:105:4-5/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TABRISI:105:4-5/r8.claim: Abu Ubayda defines ʿasif as the leaves of a crop; al-Zajjāj specifies crop leaves that were cut and eaten.
TABRISI:105:4-5/r8.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: العصف ورق الزرع قال الزجاج: أي جعلهم كورق الزرع الذي جز وأكل

THALABI:v10p296/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p296/r16.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v10p296/r16.claim: He identifies ʿaṣf as the crop's tips before it forms ears.
THALABI:v10p296/r16.anchor: قال الفراء: لا واحد لها مثل الشماطيط والعباديد والشعارير

THALABI:v10p297/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p297/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p297/r13.claim: The army was like chewed crop: beasts eat it, digest it, and scatter the dried parts, just as the soldiers' bodies were torn apart.
THALABI:v10p297/r13.anchor: فجعلهم كعصف مأكول كزرع أكلته الدواب فراثته فيبس وتفرقت أجزاؤه،

THALABI:v10p297/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p297/r14.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v10p297/r14.claim: He glosses ʿaṣf as wheat leaves.

THALABI:v10p297/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p297/r16.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p297/r16.claim: He says barley stalks were called ʿaṣf in Medina when he was a boy.
THALABI:v10p297/r16.anchor: قال الحسن: كنا ونحن غلمان بالمدينة نأكل الشعير إذا قصب وكان يسمى العصف.

THALABI:v10p297/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p297/r17.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v10p297/r17.claim: He says it is sprouted barley whose leaves are eaten.
THALABI:v10p297/r17.anchor: سعيد بن جبير: هو الشعير النابت الذي يؤكل ورقه.

THALABI:v10p297/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p297/r18.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v10p297/r18.claim: He likens the army to a mountain eaten hollow.
THALABI:v10p297/r18.anchor: عكرمة: كالجبل إذا أكل فصار أجوف.

THALABI:v10p297/r19.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p297/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p297/r19.claim: He identifies ʿaṣf as the husk enveloping a wheat grain.
THALABI:v10p297/r19.anchor: ابن عباس: هو القشر الخارج الذي يكون على حب الحنطة

THALABI:v10p297/r20.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p297/r20.speaker: المؤرخ
THALABI:v10p297/r20.claim: He calls it broken crop whose tips have fallen off.
THALABI:v10p297/r20.anchor: المؤرخ: هو ما يقصف من الزرع فسقطت أطرافه،

THALABI:v10p297/r21.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p297/r21.speaker: ابن السكيت
THALABI:v10p297/r21.claim: He groups ʿaṣf with ʿaṣīfa and jill as related terms.
THALABI:v10p297/r21.anchor: وقال ابن السكيت: هو العصف والعصيفة والجل،

THALABI:v10p297/r22.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p297/r22.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p297/r22.claim: Another gloss is crop whose grain has been eaten while its straw remains; al-Daḥḥāk glosses it as food that has been eaten.
THALABI:v10p297/r22.anchor: وقيل: كزرع قد أكل حبه وبقي تبنه، وقال الضحاك: كطعام مطعوم.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p330#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p330#2/r1.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل وعطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p330#2/r1.claim: Qatāda, Muqatil, and ʿAṭāʾ from Ibn ʿAbbās say the people became like crop straw eaten, excreted by animals, dried, and scattered, matching their dismemberment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p330#2/r1.anchor: "كزرع (وتبن) (¬1) قد أكلته الدواب، ثم راثته (¬2) (¬3) قد يبس وتفرقت أجزاؤه، شبه تقطع أوصالهم بتفرق أجزاء الروث، وهذا معنى قول قتادة (¬4)، ومقاتل (¬5)، وعطاء عن ابن عباس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p330#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p330#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p330#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan instead takes it as a crop whose grain has been eaten while its straw remains; “eaten” is understood with respect to the grain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p330#2/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: يعني جعلهم كزرع قد أكل حبه وبقى تبنه (¬7).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p330#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p330#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p330#2/r3.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk take maʾkūl to mean something fit to be eaten, so the people were like straw that animals eat.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p330#2/r3.anchor: وقيل في معنى "مأكول": إنه مما يؤكل، يعني تأكله الدواب، يقال لكل شيء يصلح للأكل: هو مأكول، [ومطعوم] (¬9). والمعنى: جعلهم كتبن تأكله الدواب، وهو معنى قول عكرمة (¬1)، (والضحاك (¬2))

WAHIDI-QT:105:5/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:105:5/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:105:5/r1.claim: The army became like crop eaten by animals, trampled, and crumbled.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:105:1-5/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:105:1-5/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:105:1-5/r6.claim: They became like crops trampled and broken after animals ate them; ‘asf’ means crop foliage.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:105:1-5/r6.anchor: كزرع أكلته الدواب فداسته وفتتته. والعصف: ورق الزرع.

ASAD-NOTES:105:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:105:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:105:intro/r1.claim: Asad dates the campaign against Mecca to 570 CE: Abyssinian Yemen’s viceroy Abrahah built a cathedral at Sana to redirect pilgrimage, then marched to destroy the Kaaba when that failed.
ASAD-NOTES:105:intro/r1.anchor: the Abyssinian campaign against Mecca in the year 570 of the Christian era. Abrahah, the Christian viceroy of the Yemen

ASAD-NOTES:105:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:105:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:105:intro/r2.claim: Abrahah’s large force included war elephants, astonishing to Arabs; it was destroyed on the march, probably by smallpox or typhus, and Abrahah died on returning to Sana.
ASAD-NOTES:105:intro/r2.anchor: Abrahah's army was totally destroyed on its march

ASAD-NOTES:105:1#n3/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:105:1#n3/r1.speaker: some authorities
ASAD-NOTES:105:1#n3/r1.claim: Some authorities regard this passage as continued in the next surah, making the two surahs one part.
ASAD-NOTES:105:1#n3/r1.anchor: This passage is evidently continued in the next surah, which, according to some authorities, is part

ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r15.claim: Asf is a noun or verbal noun connected to bending, twisting, breaking, and scattering; exegetes offer several interpretations of crop foliage.
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r15.anchor: “Asf” esasında eğip bükmek, kırıp dökmek mânalarına alâkadar olarak masdar ve isim olur bir kelimedir.

ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r16.claim: Reported glosses for asf include post-harvest leaves blown by wind and eaten by animals, broken straw, fresh leaves before the ear forms, and empty husks.
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r16.anchor: Müfessirîn bunun ekin yaprağı demek olduğunu söyleyerek birkaç vecih zikretmişlerdir

ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r17.claim: The author says the basic sense of asf is green crop foliage, which dries and breaks into straw; green immature crop cut for fodder is also called asf.
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r17.anchor: Kāmûs’ta da mezkur olduğu üzere “asf”ın asıl mânası بـَقْلُ الزَّرْعِ’dir.

ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r18.claim: Turkish calls green crop cut before maturity hasıl or kasıl, so the author chooses hasıl for asf in the translation.
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r18.anchor: Onun için biz de mealde “asf”ı “hasıl” diye terceme etmeyi muvâfık bulduk.

ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r19.claim: Meʾkul means eaten, and the crop simile has three main readings.

ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r20.speaker: Mukātil, Katâde ve Atâ
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r20.claim: The first reading compares the army to crop eaten and trampled by animals, depicting its broken, scattered state; alternatively, the result implies dung and disintegrating corpses, expressed decorously by naming the crop before its eaten result.

ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r21.speaker: İbn Cerîr ve Fahr-i Râzî
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r21.claim: Ibn Jarir and Fakhr al-Razi prefer the first reading: eaten and trampled crop, or corpses reduced and scattered like dung by euphemism.
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r21.anchor: İbn Cerîr ve Fahr-i Râzî gibi birçok müfessirîn bu vechi tercih eylemişlerdir.

ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r22.claim: The first reading also draws a decorous parallel with Qurʾān 5:75, where saying Jesus and his mother ate food euphemistically implies bodily relief.
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r22.anchor: Nitekim كَانَا يَأْكُلَانِ ٱلطَّعَامَ [el-Mâide 5/75] “Îsâ ve anası yemek yerlerdi” demek

ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r23.speaker: Zemahşerî
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r23.claim: Al-Zamakhshari appears to prefer the second, finer lexical reading: foliage eaten by worms or insects, leaving holes like the pierced bodies of the army before it could achieve its purpose.
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r23.anchor: Bu, lügat itibariyle ince bir mâna demek olduğundan Zemahşerî bunu tercih etmişe benziyor

ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r24.claim: A third reading is foliage left as empty husks after the grains are eaten; ellipsis or figurative attribution would compare the bodies or burned insides to hollow grain-pods.
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r24.anchor: Yine aynı mâna ile dâneleri yenmiş sade kapçıktan, samandan ibaret kalmış ekin yaprağı demek olur

ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r25.claim: The first reading comes most readily to mind, while asf and the Turkish hasıl both suggest foliage bent, broken, or cut while still fresh.
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r25.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh zihne tebâdür eden mâna evvelki vecihtir.

ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r26.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r26.speaker: author
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r26.claim: The causal and sequential fa in fa-jaʿalahum says the destruction followed the throwing of stones immediately and swiftly.
ELMALILI:105:1-5#4/r26.anchor: فَجَعَلَهُمْ’deki فا sebebiyetle beraber ta‘kīb ifade ettiği için, taşların remyi üzerine

ELMALILI:105:1-5#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:105:1-5#5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:105:1-5#5/r1.claim: God destroyed the arrogant army quickly and extraordinarily, laying it low like crop already eaten; the army had trusted its elephants and numbers to destroy the Kaaba without opposition.
ELMALILI:105:1-5#5/r1.anchor: Karşılarında zâhiren mukāvemet edecek bir kuvvet görmeyen, fillerine ve çokluklarına güvenerek istedikleri gibi Kâbe’yi yıkacaklarını zanneden müstevlî bir orduyu

ELMALILI:105:1-5#6/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:105:1-5#6/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:105:1-5#6/r8.claim: A sudden hail of stones from birds could injure and kill an army like crushed grain; it is unusual but possible and contains no rational contradiction, while displaying divine power.
ELMALILI:105:1-5#6/r8.anchor: Bir sahrada bir ordu üzerine ansızın bir kuş akını ve onlarla semâdan dolu gibi taş yağdırılması

ELMALILI:105:1-5#9/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:105:1-5#9/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:105:1-5#9/r13.claim: On Ikrima’s report, the eaten-straw outcome involves both the stones’ external wounds and immediate internal smallpox; stones and disease together make the event doubly extraordinary.
ELMALILI:105:1-5#9/r13.anchor: hem de o taşların tesiriyle aynı zamanda çiçek çıkartıp kırmak, iki garâbetle

ELMALILI:105:1-5#12/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:105:1-5#12/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:105:1-5#12/r13.claim: The resulting affliction could have been smallpox, measles, scarlet fever, plague, or an unknown disaster; armchair possibilities cannot identify it without experience or observation.
ELMALILI:105:1-5#12/r13.anchor: hiç bilinmedik bambaşka bir âfet oluvermesi de mümkindir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r10.claim: Verses 3–5 recount God-sent flocks of birds pelting the elephant army with baked-brick-type stones and turning them into crop remnants eaten by animals and vermin.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r10.anchor: Allah tarafından gönderilen sürülerle kuşun fil ordusunun üzerine pişkin tuğla türü taşlar yağdırarak onları nasıl hayvanlar ve haşarat tarafından yenmiş ekin artığına çevirdiğini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r13.claim: Older tafsirs treat the entire elephant event as a miracle.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r13.anchor: Eski tefsirlerde bu fil olayı bütünüyle bir mûcize olarak değerlendirilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r17.claim: The aggressor who tried to destroy God's House was punished through a miracle, while Meccans who could not resist and fled to the mountains escaped unharmed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r17.anchor: hiçbir şekilde düşmana karşı koyma imkânı bulamayan ve şehri terkedip dağlara çekilen Mekke halkı da bu olaydan zarar görmeden kurtulmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r19.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r19.claim: ʿAṣf means crop chaff and husks eaten by moths, insects, and worms and then scattered by the wind.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r19.anchor: Son âyetteki asf kelimesi ise “ekinin samanı ve buğday kapçığı gibi güve, böcek ve kurtçukların yediği, rüzgârın sağa-sola savurduğu kırıntılar” anlamına gelir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r21.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r21.claim: The final verse shows the scale of Abraha's army's calamity and its eventual destruction.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:105:1/r21.anchor: Ebrehe ve ordusunun nasıl büyük bir felâkete mâruz kaldığını ve sonuçta helâk olduğunu

CORPUSCORANICUM:105:5:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:105:5:anmerkung/r1.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:105:5:anmerkung/r1.claim: Neuwirth compares the verse with Psalms 37:1–2 and 58:8, where the wicked wither like grass, and says the episode is biblically colored.
CORPUSCORANICUM:105:5:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Neuwirth verweist als Parallele auf Psalm 37:1–2

CORPUSCORANICUM:105:5:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:105:5:anmerkung/r2.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:105:5:anmerkung/r2.claim: Neuwirth concludes that the episode is thereby biblically inflected.
CORPUSCORANICUM:105:5:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Die Episode … wird somit biblisch eingefärbt.“ (Neuwirth, Frühmekkanische Suren, 115.

CORPUSCORANICUM:105:1-5:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:105:1-5:kommentar/r1.speaker: Horovitz
CORPUSCORANICUM:105:1-5:kommentar/r1.claim: Horovitz calls Q105 the earliest example of a punishment legend.
CORPUSCORANICUM:105:1-5:kommentar/r1.anchor: Horovitz bezeichnet die Sure als das „früheste Beispiel einer Straflegende“

CORPUSCORANICUM:105:1-5:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:105:1-5:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:105:1-5:kommentar/r2.claim: Although kaid may morally evaluate the elephant army, the surah lacks the explicit charge of denial or rebellion typical of later punishment legends; its focus is God's power and protection of Mecca's sanctuary, rescue more than punishment.
CORPUSCORANICUM:105:1-5:kommentar/r2.anchor: da jedoch ein expliziter Vorwurf des „Leugnens“ oder der „Aufsässigkeit“ fehlt, wie er in späteren Straflegenden stereotyp wiederholt wird

CORPUSCORANICUM:105:1-5:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:105:1-5:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:105:1-5:kommentar/r4.claim: The surah likely invokes a familiar Meccan legend, and later Quranic punishment stories borrow its language, suggesting Q105 helped establish the genre.
CORPUSCORANICUM:105:1-5:kommentar/r4.anchor: Die Tatsache, dass spätere koranische Straferzählungen sich in der Wortwahl an Sure 105 anlehnen

CORPUSCORANICUM:105:1-5:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:105:1-5:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:105:1-5:kommentar/r5.claim: Q105 and Q106 portray human affairs, especially Mecca's fate, as subject to divine intervention rather than mere worldly causation; Allah's direct destruction of the elephant army was significant because the pre-Islamic Allah was often conceived as inactive.
CORPUSCORANICUM:105:1-5:kommentar/r5.anchor: Beide Suren insistieren, dass Gott in die Sphäre menschlichen Tuns und insbesondere in das Schicksal des mekkanischen Gemeinwesens eingreift

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p460/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p460/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p460/r2.claim: Calling the enemy eaten straw names it by its eventual fate; human stone-throwing is distinguished from God's power that completed the destruction with a stone-hurling wind.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p460/r2.anchor: a ravaging stone hurling wind on the enemy

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p373/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p373/r2.speaker: أبو المليح الهذلي
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p373/r2.claim: Abū al-Malīḥ al-Hudhalī reads فتركهم instead of فجعلهم; Ibn Jinnī says ‘left them’ implies they remained in the ruined state to which they had been reduced.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p373/r2.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: هذا على إقامة المسبب مكان السبب، إذ المراد به معنى القراءة العامة: {فجعلهم}

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p373/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p373/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p373/r3.claim: The variant can also mean ‘made them’ in the sense that those affected are left to continue in that condition; this is compatible with the common reading’s result.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p373/r3.anchor: ثم إنه قد يجوز مع هذا أن يريد به معنى الجعل الذي من حصل عليه كان معرضا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p396#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p396#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p396#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says each stone raised a lesion on an attacker, the first occurrence of smallpox; a flood then swept them into the sea.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p396#3/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال لما أرسل الله الحجارة على أصحاب الفيل

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p397/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p397/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p397/r1.claim: Qatāda identifies the eaten chaff as straw.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p397/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ كعصف مأكول ﴾ قال هو التبن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p544/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p544/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p544/r9.claim: Another explanation says the chaff is what remains after the grain is eaten, with “eaten” figuratively applied to the stalk though only its grain was consumed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p544/r9.anchor: أو الذي أكل حبه فبقي فارغا، فنسبه أنه أكل مجاز، إذ المأكول حبه لا هو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p544/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p544/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p544/r10.claim: Most read maʾkūl with a still hamza, its original passive-participle form; Abū al-Dardāʾ reportedly opens the hamza by following the preceding mīm, an anomalous pattern like maḥmūm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p544/r10.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: مأكول: بسكون الهمزة وهو الأصل، لأن صيغة مفعول من فعل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p237#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p237#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p237#2/r1.claim: Eaten chaff may be crop leaves eaten by worms or stripped of their grain; the image signifies bodies without spirits or burned insides. Another view compares their dismembered bodies to scattered dung, with Qurʾanic decorum avoiding that word; a further view makes them discarded, unprotected straw.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p237#2/r1.anchor: كورق زرع وقع فيه الاكال وهو أن يأكله الدود أوأكل حبه فبقى صفرا منه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p237#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p237#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p237#2/r2.claim: Their destruction by stones suits their attempt to destroy the Kaaba; other proposed links are the Kinani’s excrement that provoked Abraha, or fire carried by wind that burned the church.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p237#2/r2.anchor: وكأنه لما أن مجيئهم لهدم الكعبة ناسب اهلاكهم بالحجارة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p237#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p237#2/r3.speaker: أبو الدرداء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p237#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Darda is reported to read maʾkul with fatḥa on the hamza, by vowel assimilation; the author calls the reading anomalous and compares maḥmum.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p237#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو الدرداء فيما نقل ابن خالويه ماكول بفتح الهمزة اتباعا لحركة الميم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p541/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p541/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p541/r2.claim: Eaten stalks are dry, scattered crops or straw after animals eat and excrete them; their scattered parts resemble the victims' dismembered limbs.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p541/r2.anchor: كزرع وتبن أكلته الدواب فراثته فيبس وتفرقت أجزاؤه. شبه تقطع، أوصالهم بتفرق أجزاء الروث

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p541/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p541/r3.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p541/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies the stalk as wheat leaves.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p541/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p541/r4.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p541/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو التبن. وقال عكرمة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p541/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p541/r5.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p541/r5.claim: Ikrima compares it to a grain made hollow after being eaten.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p541/r5.anchor: وقال عكرمة: كالحب إذا أكل فصار أجوف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p541/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p541/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p541/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies it as the outer husk covering a wheat grain.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p541/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هو القشر الخارج الذي يكون على حب الحنطة كهيئة الغلاف له

BAYDAWI-FULL:105:2-5/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:105:2-5/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:105:2-5/r5.claim: The eaten straw may be leaves consumed by worms, husks left after their grain was eaten, or straw chewed and excreted by animals.
BAYDAWI-FULL:105:2-5/r5.anchor: كورق زرع وقع فيه، والآكال وهو أن يأكله الدود أو أكل حبه فبقي صفرا منه، أو كتين أكلته الدواب وراثته

BAYDAWI-FULL:105:2-5/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:105:2-5/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:105:2-5/r6.claim: A report promises protection from sinking into the earth and transformation during life to whoever recites the surah.
BAYDAWI-FULL:105:2-5/r6.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة الفيل أعفاه الله أيام حياته من الخسف والمسخ

BIQAI-FULL:v8p531/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p531/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p531/r8.claim: The birds' attack caused their destruction through God's creative power, since the stones' ordinary effect would not cause such mass death.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p531/r8.anchor: وكان ذلك بفعل الله سبحانه وتعالى القادر على ما أراد لأنه الذي خلق الأثر قطعا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p531/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p531/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p531/r9.claim: The image may mean leaves hollowed by worms, a grain husk emptied of its kernel, or straw eaten and excreted by livestock; the hot stones pierced from head to rear and left black cavities.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p531/r9.anchor: ورق زرع وقع فيه الأكال وهو أن يأكله الدود ويجوفه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p531/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p531/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p531/r10.claim: The Qur'anic description follows its decorum by comparing them to what has been eaten, as in the statement that Jesus and his mother ate food.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p531/r10.anchor: ولكنه جاء على ما عليه آداب القرآن كقوله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p532/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p532/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p532/r1.claim: The surah's ending and opening are joined by the wonder prompted by this extraordinary destruction, so its two ends embrace one another.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p532/r1.anchor: وهذا الإهلاك في إعجابه هو من معاني الاستفهام التقريري في أولها

DURR-FULL:v8p627/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p627/r4.speaker: عثمان بن المغيرة بن الأخنس
DURR-FULL:v8p627/r4.claim: Birds like bats pelted the army with round stones that pierced bodies; Abd al-Muttalib's scouts found the army dead, while Shahr later lost limbs and died after fleeing.
DURR-FULL:v8p627/r4.anchor: فرمتهم بحجارة مدحرجة كالبنادق تقع على رأس الرجل فتخرج من جوفه

DURR-FULL:v8p628/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p628/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p628/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas said the army camped at al-Safah; the elephant retreated from the House, and God sent birds with black, clay-coated stones that caused an itch and flesh to fall away.
DURR-FULL:v8p628/r2.anchor: كانوا لا يقدمون فيلهم إلا تأخر فدعا الله الطير الأبابيل

DURR-FULL:v8p628/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p628/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p628/r3.claim: Another Ibn Abbas report says Abraha meant to frighten the Meccans; Abd al-Muttalib prayed for the sanctuary, then birds pelted the army as the elephant bellowed and the men became eaten stalks.
DURR-FULL:v8p628/r3.anchor: اللهم إن لكل إله حلالا فامنع حلالك لا يغلبن محالهم أبدا محالك

DURR-FULL:v8p628/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p628/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p628/r4.claim: Qatada said Abraha led Ethiopians and Yemeni supporters to destroy the House over a church the Arabs had desecrated; the elephant knelt when turned toward the sanctuary.
DURR-FULL:v8p628/r4.anchor: أقبل أبرهة الأشرم بالحبشة ومن تبعه من غواة أهل اليمن

DURR-FULL:v8p630/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p630/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p630/r1.claim: Qatada's account continues: large white birds pelted the army until it became chewed stalks; Abu Yaksum survived, but his flesh fell away as he travelled home and he died.
DURR-FULL:v8p630/r1.anchor: بيضا وهي الكبيرة فجعلت ترميهم بها حتى جعلهم الله كعصف مأكول

DURR-FULL:v8p631/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p631/r2.speaker: عبيد بن عمير الليثي
DURR-FULL:v8p631/r2.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr said swallow-like birds arose from the sea, each carrying three spotted stones; they dropped them from overhead, stones pierced bodies through, and a strong wind helped destroy everyone.
DURR-FULL:v8p631/r2.anchor: بكف كل طير منها ثلاثة أحجر مجزعة في منقاره حجر وحجران في رجليه

DURR-FULL:v8p631/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p631/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p631/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas said Abu Yaksum led the attack; ababil means following one another, sijjil means clay, and the spotted agate stones tore them like rotten eaten leaves. The expedition preceded the Prophet's birth by twenty-three years.
DURR-FULL:v8p631/r4.anchor: وكانت من جزع أظفار مثل بعر الغنم

DURR-FULL:v8p632/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r1.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r1.claim: Uthman recounts a Hudhayli scout’s eyewitness report of stone-bearing birds, violent wind and darkness, and the enemy army left dead.
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r1.anchor: عن عثمان بن عفان أنه سأل رجلا من هذيل قال: أخبرني عن يوم الفيل

DURR-FULL:v8p632/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r2.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r2.claim: Abu Salih saw roughly a qafiz of the Elephant stones at Umm Hani’s house, red-striped like agate and inscribed with a man’s name and his father’s.
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r2.anchor: عن أبي صالح أنه رأى عند أم هانئ بنت أبي طالب من تلك الحجارة نحوا من قفيز

DURR-FULL:v8p632/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the defeated army’s remains as straw.
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس {فجعلهم كعصف} يقول: كالتبن

DURR-FULL:v8p632/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses the eaten chaff as wheat leaves.
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس {فجعلهم كعصف مأكول} قال: ورق الحنطة

DURR-FULL:v8p632/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r5.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr identifies the eaten chaff as wheat leaves.
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: العصف المأكول ورق الحنطة

DURR-FULL:v8p632/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r6.speaker: طاوس
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r6.claim: Tawus specifies wheat leaves perforated with holes.
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r6.anchor: عن طاوس {كعصف مأكول} قال: ورق الحنطة فيها النقب

DURR-FULL:v8p632/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r7.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r7.claim: Ikrima describes chaff eaten until it becomes hollow.
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة {كعصف مأكول} قال: إذا أكل فصار أجوف

DURR-FULL:v8p632/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the image as the birds’ chaff of crops.
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس {كعصف مأكول} قال: هو الطيور عصافة الزرع

DURR-FULL:v8p632/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r9.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r9.claim: Aisha says she saw the elephant’s keeper and driver in Mecca, both blind, disabled, and begging.
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r9.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: لقد رأيت سائس الفيل وقائده بمكة أعميين مقعدين يستطعمان

DURR-FULL:v8p632/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r10.speaker: ابن أبزى
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r10.claim: Ibn Abza reports that the Prophet was born in the Year of the Elephant.
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r10.anchor: عن ابن أبزي قال: ولد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عام الفيل

DURR-FULL:v8p632/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r11.speaker: قيس بن مخرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r11.claim: Qays ibn Makhrama says he and the Messenger were born in the Year of the Elephant.
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r11.anchor: عن قيس بن مخرمة قال: ولدت أنا ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عام الفيل

DURR-FULL:v8p632/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r12.speaker: محمد بن جبير بن مطعم
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r12.claim: Muhammad ibn Jubayr dates the Prophet’s birth to the Elephant year, ʿUkaz fifteen years later, the Kaʿba’s rebuilding at year twenty-five, and prophethood at year forty.
DURR-FULL:v8p632/r12.anchor: عن محمد بن جبير بن مطعم قال: ولد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عام الفيل

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#3/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#3/r5.claim: Araf uses “sent” rather than “sent down,” which the author says intensifies punishment; he points to the Elephant passage, where sent birds pelted them and left them like chewed straw.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#3/r5.anchor: ذلك لأن الإرسال أشد في العقوبة من الإنزال، قال تعالى في أصحاب الفيل

ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r1.claim: The defeated army is likened to eaten crop foliage: eaten by worms, or straw consumed and excreted by livestock.
ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r1.anchor: شبهوا بالعصف ورق الزرع الذي أكل ، أي وقع فيه الأكال

ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r2.claim: In keeping with Quranic propriety, the wording resembles the phrase they both ate food; it can also describe a plant whose grain was eaten and left hollow, figuratively calling the plant eaten although only its grain was consumed.
ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r2.anchor: وجاء على آداب القرآن نحو قوله : { كانا يأكلان الطعام }

ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r3.claim: The majority read maʾkūl with a quiescent hamza, the regular form of a passive participle from a verb.
ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { مأكول } : بسكون الهمزة وهو الأصل ، لأن صيغة مفعول من فعل

ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r4.speaker: أبو الدرداء
ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r4.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ, as transmitted by Ibn Khālawayh, anomalously opens the hamza by assimilation to the mīm’s vowel, like maḥmūm with an open ḥāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو الدرداء ، فيما نقل ابن خالويه : بفتح الهمزة اتباعاً لحركة الميم وهو شاذ ، وهذا كما اتبعوه في قولهم : محموم بفتح الحاء لحركة الميم

ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r5.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says that after God turned the Abyssinians away from Mecca, Arabs esteemed Quraysh as God’s people whom He defended and spared from facing their enemy; this was a divine favor.
ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r5.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق : لما رد الله الحبشة عن مكة ، عظمت العرب قريشاً وقالوا : أهل الله قاتل عنهم

ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r6.claim: Another view takes the event as an answer to Abraham’s prayer.
ABUHAYYAN:105:5/r6.anchor: وقيل : هو إجابة لدعاء الخليل عليه الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI:105:5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:105:5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:105:5/r1.claim: Al-Alusi explains the image as crop leaves eaten by worms or stripped of their grain, leaving only empty straw.
ALUSI:105:5/r1.anchor: كورق زرع وقع فيه الأكال وهو أن يأكله الدود أو أكل حبه فبقي صفراً منه

ALUSI:105:5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:105:5/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:105:5/r2.claim: On this reading, the construction either omits a governing noun and promotes its genitive complement, or uses figurative attribution.
ALUSI:105:5/r2.anchor: والكلام على هذا على حذف المضاف وإقامة المضاف إليه مقامه أو على الإسناد المجازي

ALUSI:105:5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:105:5/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:105:5/r3.claim: The comparison can reflect their spirits gone while their bodies remained, or the stones' heat burning their insides.
ALUSI:105:5/r3.anchor: والتشبيه بذلك لذهاب أرواحهم وبقاء أجسادهم أو لأن الحجر بحرارته يحرق أجوافهم

ALUSI:105:5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:105:5/r4.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI:105:5/r4.claim: Several commentators take the image as straw eaten and excreted by animals, meaning dung; the Qur'anic wording avoids that blunt term as indecorous.
ALUSI:105:5/r4.anchor: ذهب غير واحد إلى أن المعنى كتبن أكلته الدواب وراثته والمراد كروث إلا أنه لم يذكر بهذا اللفظ لهجنته فجاء على الآداب القرآنية

ALUSI:105:5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:105:5/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:105:5/r5.claim: On that interpretation, the dispersion of their severed limbs like scattered dung-pieces displays the grotesque state in which God left them.
ALUSI:105:5/r5.anchor: فشبه تقطع أوصالهم بتفرق أجزاء الروث ففيه إظهار تشويه حالهم

ALUSI:105:5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:105:5/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:105:5/r6.claim: An alternative likens them to unprotected straw that animals may eat and excrete: they were discarded, ignored, and left in the desert for animals, with no one to gather or bury them.
ALUSI:105:5/r6.anchor: وقيل المعنى كتبن تأكله الدواب وتروثه والمراد جعلهم في حكم التبن الذي لا يمنع عنه الدواب أي مبتذلين ضائعين

ALUSI:105:5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:105:5/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:105:5/r7.claim: Al-Alusi finds the explanation strained that مأكول replaces “animals ate it” to cast a past event as present.
ALUSI:105:5/r7.anchor: إلا أنه وضع مأكول موضع أكلته الدواب لحكاية الماضي في صورة الحال وهو كما ترى

ALUSI:105:5/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:105:5/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:105:5/r8.claim: Because they came to demolish the Kaʿba, it was fitting that they be destroyed by stones.
ALUSI:105:5/r8.anchor: لما أن مجيئهم لهدم الكعبة ناسب إهلاكهم بالحجارة

ALUSI:105:5/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:105:5/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:105:5/r9.claim: If al-Kinani's excrement provoked their anger, their punishment's likeness to dung is apt under the dung interpretation.
ALUSI:105:5/r9.anchor: الذي أثار غضبهم عذرة الكناني شبههم فيما فعل سبحانه بهم على القول الأخير بالروث

ALUSI:105:5/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:105:5/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:105:5/r10.claim: Al-Alusi also speculates that the incident involved the Kaʿba burning from fire carried by the wind from Arab fires; this background suits the image of chaff after its grain is eaten.
ALUSI:105:5/r10.anchor: الذي أثاره احتراقها بما حملته الريح من نار العرب على ما سمعت شبههم عز وجل فيما فعل جل شأنه بهم بعصف أكل حبه

ALUSI:105:5/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:105:5/r11.speaker: أبو الدرداء
ALUSI:105:5/r11.claim: As transmitted by Ibn Khalawayh, Abu al-Darda reads مأكول with fatḥa on the hamza through vowel assimilation to the mīm; Al-Alusi calls it anomalous and compares the assimilation to محموم, where ḥā follows mīm's vowel.
ALUSI:105:5/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو الدرداء فيما نقل ابن خالويه مأكول بفتح الهمزة اتباعاً لحركة الميم وهو شاذ وهذا كما أتبعوا في قولهم محموم الحاء لحركة الميم

BAGHAWI:105:5/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:105:5/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:105:5/r1.claim: They became like crops or straw eaten by animals and excreted, then dried and scattered; the scattering of their limbs is likened to the dispersed parts of dung.
BAGHAWI:105:5/r1.anchor: كزرع وتبن أكلته الدواب فراثته ، فيبس وتفرقت أجزاؤه . شبه تقطع أوصالهم بتفرق أجزاء الروث

BAGHAWI:105:5/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:105:5/r2.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI:105:5/r2.claim: Mujahid says ʿaṣf means wheat leaves.

BAGHAWI:105:5/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:105:5/r4.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI:105:5/r4.claim: ʿIkrima compares it to grain eaten until it is hollow.
BAGHAWI:105:5/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة : كالحب إذا أكل فصار أجوف

BAGHAWI:105:5/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:105:5/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:105:5/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says it is the outer husk that forms a covering around the wheat kernel.
BAGHAWI:105:5/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : هو القشر الخارج الذي يكون على حب الحنطة كهيئة الغلاف له

BAYDAWI:105:5/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:105:5/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:105:5/r1.claim: The army became like crop leaves eaten by worms, or like stalks whose grain was eaten away leaving them hollow.
BAYDAWI:105:5/r1.anchor: فجعلهم كعصف مأكول } كورق زرع وقع فيه والأكال وهو أن يأكله الدود ، أو أكل حبه فبقي صفرا منه ،

BAYDAWI:105:5/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:105:5/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:105:5/r2.claim: Another comparison is to dried figs eaten and excreted by livestock.

BIQAI:105:5/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:105:5/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:105:5/r1.claim: God alone caused their destruction and created the effect, since such projectiles would not ordinarily produce the extraordinary devastation described.
BIQAI:105:5/r1.anchor: وكان ذلك بفعل الله سبحانه وتعالى القادر على ما أراد ؛ لأنه الذي خلق الأثر قطعاً ؛ لأن مثله لا ينشأ عنه ما نشأ من الهلاك

BIQAI:105:5/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:105:5/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:105:5/r2.claim: The image can mean crop leaves eaten by worms and hollowed out; the hot, forceful stones pierced bodies from head to anus, leaving blackened tunnels.
BIQAI:105:5/r2.anchor: ورق زرع وقع فيه الأكال ، وهو أن يأكله الدود ويجوفه ؛ لأن الحجر كان يأتي في الرأس فيخرق بما له من الحرارة

BIQAI:105:5/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:105:5/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:105:5/r3.claim: Other explanations are a grain eaten away and left hollow, or straw eaten and excreted by animals.
BIQAI:105:5/r3.anchor: أو أكل حبة فبقي صفراً منه ، أو كتبن أكلته الدواب وراثته

BIQAI:105:5/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:105:5/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:105:5/r4.claim: The euphemistic wording follows Qurʾānic decorum, as when Mary and Jesus are described as eating food rather than by the bodily outcome implied here.

BIQAI:105:5/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:105:5/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:105:5/r5.claim: The marvel of the destruction answers the sūra’s opening rhetorical question, joining its two ends.
BIQAI:105:5/r5.anchor: وهذا الإهلاك في إعجابه هو من معاني الاستفهام التقريري في أولها ، فقد تعانق طرفاها ، والتف أخراها بأولاها

DURR:105:5/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:105:5/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:105:5/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “asf” as straw or chaff.
DURR:105:5/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس { فجعلهم كعصف } يقول : كالتبن

DURR:105:5/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:105:5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:105:5/r2.claim: In another report, Ibn Abbas glosses the eaten chaff as wheat leaves.
DURR:105:5/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس { فجعلهم كعصف مأكول } قال : ورق الحنطة

DURR:105:5/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:105:5/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:105:5/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr also says the eaten chaff is wheat leaves.
DURR:105:5/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال : العصف المأكول ورق الحنطة

DURR:105:5/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:105:5/r4.speaker: طاوس
DURR:105:5/r4.claim: Tawus explains it as wheat leaves riddled with holes.
DURR:105:5/r4.anchor: عن طاوس { كعصف مأكول } قال : ورق الحنطة فيها النقب

DURR:105:5/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:105:5/r5.speaker: عكرمة
DURR:105:5/r5.claim: Ikrima says the plant becomes hollow after it is eaten.
DURR:105:5/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة { كعصف مأكول } قال : إذا أكل فصار أجوف

DURR:105:5/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:105:5/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:105:5/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses the image as birds and crop chaff.
DURR:105:5/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس { كعصف مأكول } قال : هو الطيور عصافة الزرع

DURR:105:5/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:105:5/r7.speaker: عائشة
DURR:105:5/r7.claim: Aisha says she saw the elephant's handler and driver in Mecca, both blind, crippled, and begging.
DURR:105:5/r7.anchor: عن عائشة قالت : لقد رأيت سائس الفيل وقائده بمكة أعميين مقعدين يستطعمان

DURR:105:5/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:105:5/r8.speaker: ابن أبزى
DURR:105:5/r8.claim: Ibn Abza says the Prophet was born in the Year of the Elephant.
DURR:105:5/r8.anchor: عن ابن أبزى قال : ولد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عام الفيل

DURR:105:5/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:105:5/r9.speaker: قيس بن مخرمة
DURR:105:5/r9.claim: Qays ibn Makhrama says that he and the Prophet were born in the Year of the Elephant.
DURR:105:5/r9.anchor: عن قيس بن مخرمة قال : ولدت أنا ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عام الفيل

DURR:105:5/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:105:5/r10.speaker: محمد بن جبير بن مطعم
DURR:105:5/r10.claim: Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im says the Prophet was born in the Elephant year; Ukaz occurred 15 years later, the Kaaba was built 25 years later, and prophethood began 40 years from that year.
DURR:105:5/r10.anchor: عن محمد بن جبير بن مطعم قال : ولد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عام الفيل ، وكانت عكاظ بعد الفيل بخمس عشرة سنة

IBNATIYYA:105:5/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r1.claim: ʿAṣf means wheat leaves and straw; Ibn ʿAṭiyya cites ʿAlqama ibn ʿAbada’s verse as usage evidence for ʿuṣayfa.
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r1.anchor: و «العصف » : ورق الحنطة وتبنه ،   ومنه قول علقمة بن عبدة : [ البسيط ] تسقى مذانب قد مالت عصيفتها

IBNATIYYA:105:5/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r2.claim: They became vanishing clay like wheat leaves eaten and passed by animals; the image combines humiliation, baseness, and destruction.
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r2.anchor: والمعنى صاروا طيناً ذاهباً كورق حنطة أكلته الدواب وراثته

IBNATIYYA:105:5/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r3.speaker: أبو الخليج الهذلي
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r3.claim: Abū al-Khalīj al-Hudhalī reads fataraktahum in place of fa-jaʿalahum.
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو الخليج الهذلي{[11992]}  " فتركتهم كعصف "

IBNATIYYA:105:5/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r4.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r4.claim: Some read fajaʿalat-hum, with a still tāʾ and fatḥa on the lām, taking the birds as the feminine subject that made them like eaten straw.
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r4.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم : «فجعلتهم » يعنون الطير بفتح اللام وتاء ساكنة

IBNATIYYA:105:5/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r5.claim: ʿIkrima says ʿaṣf is grain that becomes hollow after being eaten.
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r5.anchor: وقال عكرمة : العصف حب البر إذا أكل فصار أجوف

IBNATIYYA:105:5/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r6.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says ʿaṣf is the tips of crops before they form ears.
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء : هو أطراف الزرع قبل أن يسنبل

IBNATIYYA:105:5/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r7.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r7.claim: In Ubayy ibn Kaʿb’s codex, this sūra runs directly into Sūrat Quraysh without a separation.
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r7.anchor: وهذه السورة متصلة في مصحف أبي بن كعب بسورة { لإيلاف قريش } لا فصل بينهما

IBNATIYYA:105:5/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r8.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r8.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna says their imam recited the two sūras continuously as one sūra.
IBNATIYYA:105:5/r8.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة : كان لنا إمام يقرأ بهما متصلة سورة واحدة

IBNKATHIR:105:5/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r4.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r4.claim: Ibn Hishām defines ʿaṣf as uncut crop leaves and gives ʿaṣafa as its singular.
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r4.anchor: والعصفُ : ورقُ الزرع الذي لم يُقضب ، واحدته عصفة

IBNKATHIR:105:5/r21.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r21.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r21.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr says ʿaṣf is straw, called habūr by ordinary people.
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r21.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير : يعني التبن الذي تسميه العامة : هبور

IBNKATHIR:105:5/r22.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r22.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r22.claim: In another report, Saʿīd b. Jubayr identifies ʿaṣf as wheat leaves.
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r22.anchor: وفي رواية عن سعيد : ورق الحنطة

IBNKATHIR:105:5/r23.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r23.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r23.claim: Saʿīd also glosses ʿaṣf as straw and maʾkūl as qasīl cut for animals; al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī agrees.
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r23.anchor: وعنه أيضا : العصف : التبن . والمأكول : القصيل يجز للدواب . وكذلك قال الحسن البصري

IBNKATHIR:105:5/r24.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r24.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r24.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says ʿaṣf is the husk on a grain, like the covering on wheat.
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r24.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : العصف : القشرة التي على الحبة ، كالغلاف على الحنطة

IBNKATHIR:105:5/r25.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r25.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r25.claim: Ibn Zayd defines ʿaṣf as crop and vegetable leaves after animals eat and excrete them, leaving dry refuse.
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r25.anchor: وقال ابن زيد : العصف : ورق الزرع ، وورق البقل ، إذا أكلته البهائم فراثته ، فصار درينا

IBNKATHIR:105:5/r26.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r26.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r26.claim: God utterly destroyed the army, frustrated their plot and rage, and left them no gain; most died and every survivor returned wounded.
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r26.anchor: والمعنى : أن الله ، سبحانه وتعالى ، أهلكهم ودمرهم ، وردهم بكيدهم وغيظهم لم ينالوا خيرًا ، وأهلك عامتهم

IBNKATHIR:105:5/r31.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r31.speaker: أبو نعيم
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r31.claim: Abū Nuʿaym transmits a very unusual account that Abraha sent Shamir b. Mafṣūd with 20,000 men, without going himself; birds struck at night and the army lay dead by morning. Abū Nuʿaym preferred this account.
