IBNKATHIR:105:5/r31.anchor: وقد ذكر الحافظ أبو نعيم في كتاب " دلائل النبوة " من طريق ابن وهب

IBNKATHIR:105:5/r35.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r35.speaker: أبو قيس بن الأسلت الأنصاري المري
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r35.claim: Abū Qays b. al-Aslat’s poem describes the elephant’s mutilation, the army’s flight, and a shower of stones that enveloped them as they bleated like sheep.
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r35.anchor: وقال أبو قيس{[30549]}  بن الأسلت الأنصاري المري

IBNKATHIR:105:5/r36.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r36.speaker: أبو الصلت بن أبي ربيعة
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r36.claim: A poem attributed to Abū al-Ṣalt, also ascribed to Umayya b. Abī al-Ṣalt, describes the elephant halted at al-Mughammas, the army’s flight and broken bones, and the enduring ḥanīf faith.
IBNKATHIR:105:5/r36.anchor: وقال أبو الصلت بن أبي ربيعة الثقفي ، ويروى لأمية بن أبي الصلت

MAWARDI:105:5/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:105:5/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:105:5/r1.claim: ʿAṣf is crop leaves, and eaten means eaten by worms.
MAWARDI:105:5/r1.anchor: أن العصف ورق الزَّرع ،   والمأكول الذي قد أكله الدود ،   قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI:105:5/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:105:5/r2.speaker: حسين بن ثابت
MAWARDI:105:5/r2.anchor: أن العصف المأكول هو الطعام ،   وهذا قول حسين بن ثابت

MAWARDI:105:5/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:105:5/r3.speaker: عطاء بن السائب
MAWARDI:105:5/r3.claim: The eaten ʿaṣf is the wheat husk after its contents have been eaten.
MAWARDI:105:5/r3.anchor: أنه قشر الحنطة إذا أكل ما فيه ،   رواه عطاء بن السائب

MAWARDI:105:5/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:105:5/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI:105:5/r4.claim: The eaten ʿaṣf is a vegetable leaf after livestock eat and pass it.
MAWARDI:105:5/r4.anchor: أنه ورق البقل إذا أكلته البهائم فراثته ،   قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI:105:5/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:105:5/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والحسن
MAWARDI:105:5/r5.claim: ʿAṣf means straw or chaff, while the eaten material is fresh fodder fed to livestock.
MAWARDI:105:5/r5.anchor: أن العصف التبن ،   والمأكول القصيل للدواب ،   قاله سعيد بن جبير والحسن

MAWARDI:105:5/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:105:5/r6.speaker: قوم
MAWARDI:105:5/r6.claim: Some said the event was a miracle for a prophet of that era, suggesting Khālid ibn Sinān as that prophet.
MAWARDI:105:5/r6.anchor: فقال قوم : كان ذلك معجزة لنبيّ كان في ذلك الزمان ،   وقيل : إنه كان خالد بن سنان

MAWARDI:105:5/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:105:5/r7.speaker: آخرون
MAWARDI:105:5/r7.claim: Others said the event prepared the way for Muhammad’s prophethood because he was born in its year, or on the very day.
MAWARDI:105:5/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل كان تمهيداً وتوطيداً لنبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ؛ لأنه ولد في عامه ،   وقيل : في يومه

NASAFI:105:5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:105:5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:105:5/r1.claim: The people were made like crop eaten by worms.
NASAFI:105:5/r1.anchor: { فَجَعَلَهُمْ كَعَصْفٍ مَّأْكُولِ } زرع أكله الدود

QURTUBI:105:5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:105:5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:105:5/r1.claim: God made the People of the Elephant like crop leaves eaten by animals and spat out below; their broken limbs resembled the scattered pieces of fodder.
QURTUBI:105:5/r1.anchor: أي جعل الله أصحاب الفيل كورق الزرع إذا أكلته الدواب ، فرمت به من أسفل . شبه تقطع أوصالهم بتفرق أجزائه .

QURTUBI:105:5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:105:5/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI:105:5/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd and others are reported to have transmitted this explanation of the verse.
QURTUBI:105:5/r2.anchor: روى معناه عن ابن زيد وغيره

QURTUBI:105:5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:105:5/r3.speaker: علقمة
QURTUBI:105:5/r3.claim: Alqama's verse uses asifa for the foliage gathered around the grain head, supporting the sense of asf as crop leaves.
QURTUBI:105:5/r3.anchor: ومما يدل على أنه ورق الزرع قول علقمة : تسقي مذانب قد مالت عصيفتها

QURTUBI:105:5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:105:5/r4.speaker: رؤبة بن العجاج
QURTUBI:105:5/r4.claim: Ru'ba's poem recounts the Elephant army struck by stones and flocks of birds, ending by saying they became like eaten chaff.
QURTUBI:105:5/r4.anchor:
وقال رؤبة بن العجاج :
ومسهم ما مس أصحاب الفيل

QURTUBI:105:5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:105:5/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:105:5/r5.claim: Asf is a collective noun whose singular forms include asfa, asafa, and asifa.
QURTUBI:105:5/r5.anchor: العصف : جمع ، واحدته عصفة وعصافة ، وعصيفة .

QURTUBI:105:5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:105:5/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI:105:5/r6.claim: The kaf is used for comparison alongside mithl, as in 42:11, where nothing is like Him.
QURTUBI:105:5/r6.anchor: للتشبيه مع مثل ، نحو قوله تعالى : { ليس كمثله شيء }

QURTUBI:105:5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:105:5/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI:105:5/r7.claim: Ma'kul means that its grain was eaten, just as calling someone handsome means that his face is handsome.
QURTUBI:105:5/r7.anchor: كقشر الحنطة إذا خرجت منه الحبة

QURTUBI:105:5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:105:5/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:105:5/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says the comparison is to wheat chaff: the husk surrounding the wheat kernel.
QURTUBI:105:5/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : { فجعلهم كعصف مأكول } أن المراد به قشر البر

QURTUBI:105:5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:105:5/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI:105:5/r9.claim: A report says a stone would strike a man and bring out everything inside him, leaving him like wheat husk after the kernel is removed.
QURTUBI:105:5/r9.anchor: ويروى أن الحجر كان يقع على أحدهم فيخرج كل ما في جوفه ، فيبقى كقشر الحنطة

QURTUBI:105:5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:105:5/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI:105:5/r10.claim: Ibn Masud says God sent wind to strike the birds' stones and strengthen them, so everyone struck died; only one man from Kinda survived.
QURTUBI:105:5/r10.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود : لما رمت الطير بالحجارة ، بعث الله ريحا فضربت الحجارة فزادتها شدة

QURTUBI:105:5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:105:5/r11.speaker: رجل من كندة
QURTUBI:105:5/r11.claim: The surviving man from Kinda's poem recalls the birds, a passing cloud, and the disaster that befell the army at al-Mughammas.
QURTUBI:105:5/r11.anchor: خشيت الله إذ قد بث طيرا

QURTUBI:105:5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:105:5/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI:105:5/r12.claim: Another report says the birds did not strike all the army, only those God willed; Qurtubi leaves the matter to God.

QURTUBI:105:5/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:105:5/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI:105:5/r13.claim: Qurtubi adds that the commander and a small remnant returned, then died after telling others what they had seen.
QURTUBI:105:5/r13.anchor: وقد تقدم أن أميرهم رجع وشرذمة لطيفة معه

QURTUBI:105:5/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:105:5/r14.speaker: ابن إسحاق
QURTUBI:105:5/r14.claim: Ibn Ishaq says God's repelling the Abyssinians made Arabs honor Quraysh as God's people, believing God had fought for them and spared them the enemy; this was a divine favor.
QURTUBI:105:5/r14.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق : لما رد الله الحبشة عن مكة ، عظمت العرب قريشا وقالوا : أهل الله ، قاتل عنهم

RAZI:105:5/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:105:5/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:105:5/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī refers readers to his earlier discussion of al-ʿaṣf in 55:12, 'grain with husk and fragrant plants.'
RAZI:105:5/r1.anchor: ذكرناها في قوله : { والحب ذو العصف }

RAZI:105:5/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:105:5/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:105:5/r2.claim: One explanation of al-ʿaṣf is crop leaves left after harvest, blown about and eaten by livestock.
RAZI:105:5/r2.anchor: أنه ورق الزرع الذي يبقى في الأرض بعد الحصاد وتعصفه الرياح فتأكله المواشي

RAZI:105:5/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:105:5/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI:105:5/r3.claim: Abū Muslim takes al-ʿaṣf as straw, citing 55:12: wind scatters it from the grain at winnowing; once eaten it is destroyed and offers no protection or return.
RAZI:105:5/r3.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : العصف التبن لقوله : { ذو العصف والريحان }

RAZI:105:5/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:105:5/r4.speaker: الفراء
RAZI:105:5/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains al-ʿaṣf as the tips of the crop before its grain head ripens.
RAZI:105:5/r4.anchor: قال الفراء : هو أطراف الزرع قبل أن يدرك السنبل

RAZI:105:5/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:105:5/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:105:5/r5.claim: Another explanation is grain whose kernel has been eaten, leaving its husk.
RAZI:105:5/r5.anchor: هو الحب الذي أكل لبه وبقي قشره

RAZI:105:5/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:105:5/r6.speaker: مقاتل وقتادة وعطاء عن ابن عباس
RAZI:105:5/r6.claim: The phrase can mean crops eaten by animals, excreted as dung, then dried and scattered; the army's severed limbs are likened to the dung's disintegration, expressed euphemistically in Qur'anic diction, as in 5:75.
RAZI:105:5/r6.anchor: كانا يأكلان الطعام } وهو قول مقاتل ، وقتادة وعطاء عن ابن عباس

RAZI:105:5/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:105:5/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:105:5/r7.claim: A second possibility under 'eaten' is crop leaves damaged by worms.
RAZI:105:5/r7.anchor: أن يكون التشبيه واقعا بورق الزرع إذا وقع فيه الآكال

RAZI:105:5/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:105:5/r8.speaker: الحسن
RAZI:105:5/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the phrase as crop whose grain has been eaten and whose straw remains; 'eaten' attaches to the crop by understood ellipsis, as when 'beautiful' means beautiful-faced.
RAZI:105:5/r8.anchor: لأن هذا المعنى معلوم وهذا قول الحسن

RAZI:105:5/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:105:5/r9.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
RAZI:105:5/r9.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk take maʾkūl to mean edible or fit to be eaten: the people were like straw livestock consume.
RAZI:105:5/r9.anchor: والمعنى جعلهم كتبن تأكله الدواب وهو قول عكرمة والضحاك

RAZI:105:5/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:105:5/r10.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI:105:5/r10.claim: Some argued that al-Ḥajjāj destroyed the Kaaba without a similar event, and thus the Elephant incident either did not occur as described or had another motive than honoring the Kaaba.
RAZI:105:5/r10.anchor: قال بعضهم : إن الحجاج خرب الكعبة ، ولم يحدث شيء من ذلك

RAZI:105:5/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:105:5/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:105:5/r11.claim: Al-Rāzī answers that the Elephant event was an irhāṣ, a portent needed before Muhammad's advent; after his prophethood was established by decisive proofs, no such sign was needed.
RAZI:105:5/r11.anchor: وقع إرهاصا لأمر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ، والإرهاص إنما يحتاج إليه قبل قدومه

TAB:105:5/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:105:5/r1.speaker: author
TAB:105:5/r1.claim: God made the People of the Elephant like crops eaten by animals and excreted, then dried and scattered; their punished limbs and bodies were torn and dispersed like the excrement’s fragments.
TAB:105:5/r1.anchor: فجعل الله أصحاب الفيل كزرع أكلته الدوابّ فراثته ،   فيبس وتفرّقت أجزاؤه ،   شبّه تقطّع أوصالهم بالعقوبة التي نزلت بهم

TAB:105:5/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:105:5/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TAB:105:5/r2.claim: Some say ʿasf is the outer husk on a wheat grain, like a covering around it.
TAB:105:5/r2.anchor: وقد كان بعضهم يقول :  العَصْف :  هو القشر الخارج الذي يكون على حبّ الحنطة من خارج ،   كهيئة الغلاف لها .

TAB:105:5/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:105:5/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:105:5/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies ʿasf as wheat leaves or straw.
TAB:105:5/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   قوله :  {  كَعَصْفٍ مأْكُولٍ } قال :  ورق الحنطة .

TAB:105:5/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:105:5/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB:105:5/r4.anchor: عن قتادة {  كَعَصْفٍ مأْكُولٍ }قال :  هو التّبن .

TAB:105:5/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:105:5/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:105:5/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the phrase as a crop that has been eaten.
TAB:105:5/r5.anchor: سمعت أبا معاذ ،   قال :  أخبرنا عبيد ،   قال :  سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله :  {  كَعَصْفٍ مأْكُولٍ } :  كزرع مأكول .

TAB:105:5/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:105:5/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:105:5/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak gives a Nabataean term for ʿasf, al-habur, with an alternate transmitted form, al-maqhur.
TAB:105:5/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك ،   في قوله {  كَعَصْفٍ مأْكُولٍ } قال :  هو الهَبُور بالنبطية ،   وفي رواية :  المقهور .

TAB:105:5/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:105:5/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:105:5/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies ʿasf as crop and vegetable leaves that beasts eat and excrete until they become dung.
TAB:105:5/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  {  فَجَعَلَهُمْ كَعَصْفٍ مأْكُولٍ } قال :  ورق الزرع وورق البقل ،   إذا أكلته البهائم فراثته

TAB:105:5/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:105:5/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:105:5/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says the wheat is eaten and its ʿasf blown away by the wind; ʿasf is the husk above the wheat.
TAB:105:5/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس {  كَعَصْفٍ مأْكُولٍ } قال :  البُرّ يؤكل ويُلْقى عَصْفُه الريح .   والعَصْف :  الذي يكون فوق البرّ :  هو لحاء البرّ .

TAB:105:5/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:105:5/r9.speaker: حبيب بن أبي ثابت
TAB:105:5/r9.claim: Habib ibn Abi Thabit glosses the phrase as food that has been eaten.
TAB:105:5/r9.anchor: عن حبيب بن أبي ثابت :  {  كَعَصْفٍ مأْكُولٍ } قال :  كطعام مطعوم .

BURHAN:v1p186/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p186/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p186/r1.claim: One sign of coherence between consecutive sūras is a verbal link: the end of al-Fīl, 'like eaten straw,' connects to the opening of Quraysh.
BURHAN:v1p186/r1.anchor: ومن أسراره مناسبة فاتحة السورة بخاتمة التى قبلها حتى إن منها ما يظهر تعلقها به لفظا

BURHAN:v2p304/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p304/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p304/r5.claim: The comparison to eaten straw euphemizes the people ending up as dung, since eaten leaves eventually reach that state.
BURHAN:v2p304/r5.anchor: كنى به عن مصيرهم إلى العذرة فان الورق اذا اكل انتهى حاله إلى ذلك

ITQAN:v3p296/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p296/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p296/r5.claim: A surah's opening may connect verbally with the preceding surah's close; the Elephant's “eaten straw” is followed by Quraysh's “for the security of Quraysh.”
ITQAN:v3p296/r5.anchor: ومنه مناسبة فاتحة السورة لخاتمة ما قبلها حتى أن منها

ITQAN:v3p296/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p296/r6.speaker: الأخفش
ITQAN:v3p296/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash describes the connection between the Elephant's ending and Quraysh's opening as a syntactic connection, like “so that they might be enemies and grief” in the Moses story.
ITQAN:v3p296/r6.anchor: فقد قال الأخفش اتصالها بها من باب

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p234/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p234/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p234/r4.claim: God destroyed the people of the elephant when they sought to demolish the Kaaba and move its stones to Yemen for a rival sanctuary, preserving Quraysh's residence and honor beside the House.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p234/r4.anchor: قصد أصحاب الفيل إلى مكة ليهدموا الكعبة
